rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: A speech or music signal changes too slowly to be radiated from a practical antenna. Modulation copies that message onto a high-frequency carrier so the antenna can be a reasonable length.  ·  In amplitude modulation the carrier frequency stays constant and the amplitude rises and falls with the message. A louder message makes a deeper variation, up to the point where the envelope would cross zero.  ·  The modulated wave contains the carrier and two sidebands, one at f_c + f_m and one at f_c − f_m. If the highest message frequency is f_m, the bandwidth occupied is 2 f_m.
